give it here! phrase

also hand it over, pass it here, tell me

classical

Traupman 99, 104
Ter. Ph. 950: Nōlō, volō; volō, nōlō rūrsum; cedo, cape
Plaut. Most. 373b: Vigilō, cedo bibam

1Cedo, cette: short e and short final o, so no macrons. Lewis & Short marks it cĕdo and lists it apart from cēdō, cēdere (“go, give way”); de Vaan s.v. cedo, an imperative (“give, tell”). Ruling: cedo with short vowels.

Cedo!1 (plural cette)

give it here! hand it over! tell me!

An old imperative from -ce + the root of dō; it takes an object. Not cēdō, cēdere “go, give way”.

Examples

  • Cedo manum.

    give me your handPlaut. Capt. 859, Most. 332

  • Cedo istum lapidem!

    Give me that stone!composed

  • Cette manūs, ambō; viam trānsīmus.

    Give me your hands, both of you; we’re crossing the road.composed

See also here you are.
